DILG BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT D\LG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.qov.ph OILG OPINION NO. s. 20ß_ MAY 15 2025 JOHN ANDRE SEREVO iohnandreserevo@gmail.com Dear Mr. Serevo: This has reference to your letter dated 19 March 2024 requesting this department's legal opinion on whether a local government unit (LGU) may implement restrictions without supporting or enabling laws. Per your representation, you were apprehended by the Traffic Management Office of your LGU for driving your Electric Bicycle (E-Bike) along Government Halili Avenue, a national highway. You represented that the violation was for "unauthorized driving of E-bike along the highway", and you also mentioned that there was no ordinance yet disallowing e-bikes in Government Halili Ave. You mentioned that the traffic enforcer explained that they apprehended you since they were just trying to make the streets safer because of the previous accidents caused by E-bikes. However, you also stated that the traffic enforcers cannot provide for a legal basis for your apprehension. Thus, the request for legal opinion. At the onset, we invite your attention to Section 16 of R.A. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991, to wit: "Section 16. General Welfare. - Every local government unit shall exercise the powers expressly qranted. those necessarily implied therefrom. as well as powers necessary. appropriate. or incidental for its efficient and effective qovernance. and those which are essential to the promotion of the qeneral welfare. Within their respective territorial jurisdictions, local government units shall ensure and support, among other things, the preservation and enrichment of culture, promote health and safety, enhance the right of the people to a balanced ecology, encourage and support the development of appropriate and self-reliant scientific and technological capabilities, improve public morals, enhance economic prosperity and social justice, promote full employment among their residents, maintain peace and order, and preserve the comfort and convenience of their inhabitants." The foregoing provides for the general welfare clause and the police power of the LGUs. Police power is the authority to prescribe regulations to promote the health, morals, peace, education, good order, safety, and general welfare of the people. As an inherent attribute of sovereignty, police power primarily rests with the State. In "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

furtherance of the State's policy to foster genuine and meaningful local autonomy, the national legislature delegated the exercise of police power to local government units (LGUs) as agents of the State. Such delegation can be found in Section 16 of the LGC, which embodies the general welfare clause. 1 Since LGUs exercise delegated police power as agents of the State, it is incumbent upon them to act in conformity to the will of their principal, the State.2 However, we would like to draw your attention to Section 3 of the Land Transportation Office (L TO) Administrative Order No. 2021-039, which outlines the "Consolidated Guidelines in the Classification, Registration, and Operation of All Types of Electric Motor Vehicles" and specifies the type, category, and types of roads on which Electric Motor Vehicles are permitted. Please note that, as stated in the aforementioned LTO Administrative Order, not all Electric Motor Vehicles are permitted to operate on National Highways. Only Category L4 and higher3 electric vehicles have limited access to tertiary national routes. In the matter at hand, it is unclear what type or category of Electric Motor Vehicle was seized along Government Halili Avenue, a national highway. Thus, we are of the considered view that your apprehension was based on LTO Administrative Order No. 2021-039. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. Further, this is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion rendered by more competent authorities and/or the courts. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY. ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLNRPB,'LLLS-LRALLDnasm City of Batangas V.
